rules.rule: Activity combines own-history percentile families: Attention (CryptoPanic news counts and LunarCrush social counts, and X once registered), Trading activity (Spec-1's trading_activity_turnover_24h and trading_activity_abs_return_24h, backfilled hourly with Price action) and Leverage (derivatives_oi_change_24h_1h, optional, live only).
Each input becomes the mid-rank percentile of its current value in the coin's own window of up to 90 days, no winsorising; under 20 non-zero days of history an input is unknown, never 0 or 50.

While X is not collected, Attention is news_cryptopanic_posts_24h_1h and social_lunarcrush_posts_24h_1h, each the mid-rank percentile in its own window, combined inside the family by Stouffer's rule at equal weights: 1/2 each when both are measured, 1 for the one measured when the other is not, and Attention is Not measured when neither is. X's input x_posts_24h_1h is unknown at weight 0 and named on /method. In A each measured family carries 1/k of the combination, k the number of measured families (Trading activity always among them), so a measured input's weight in A is 1/(2k) or 1/k.

Families combine by Stouffer's rule as Spec-1's T2.0 does (equal weights inside a family; normal scores summed over the root of their count); A publishes with Trading activity measured, else Not measured with the reason; Attention and Leverage join when measured.

A is the percentile of the combination among the coin universe's 90 days of daily references (hashed), read in seven words (Very quiet to Very busy, about 5% Very busy daily by construction once the reference is all live); ink density only, no direction word, no colour of direction, no /derivatives.

While the news collector is down (no news-counts run scheduled in the 120 minutes before a reading's slot passed by the reading run's start), news_cryptopanic_posts_24h_1h is unknown at weight 0 with reason not_collected, as X's input is; no news value is carried forward, invented or read as 0. News rejoins at the first reading after a news-counts run passes again, under the percentiles and freshness rules.

While the social collector is down (no social-counts run scheduled in the 120 minutes before a reading's slot passed by the reading run's start), social_lunarcrush_posts_24h_1h is unknown at weight 0 with reason not_collected; it rejoins at the first reading after a social-counts run passes again. Attention shows Not measured only when both its inputs are not measured.

Activity's numbers wait for 48 hours of green capture (§10.4): the last 96 capture-markets slots at :15 and :45 all passed; news-counts and social-counts runs do not gate publication (rules news_not_collected and social_not_collected). The numbers are flagged until 4 Feb 2027 (backfilled Trading activity history); a reading's receipt names origin and backfillEnd where its window holds backfilled rows.
A change to A1.0 needed before 1 Mar 2027 opens A1.0's epoch 1, closing its earlier sample unpooled; shared lists (exclusions, universe) count for both engines.

changes: attention.news rule pacing: one request per 10 seconds or slower, each a single attempt with no retry on 429, 5xx or timeout (was one per 5 seconds with backoff on 429).

attention.news rule canary_and_failures: an empty object at HTTP 200 is a fetched window with zero articles when the same run's bitcoin request has already parsed with at least one article; otherwise it stays a failed request, null and never 0 (was always a failed request).
amendments.disclosure: Spec-2 amendment 1 (10 Nov 2026), before any evaluation data and before any news count was written: the GDELT news-stories job now sends one request per 10 seconds, each a single attempt with no retry, and reads an empty GDELT reply as a window with no articles only when the same run's bitcoin canary request returned at least one article; otherwise that window stays failed and null, never 0. The job had not passed since it started (10 Nov: 109 of 241 requests in three hours were rate-limited, 54 were empty replies). The queries, the publisher allowlist, the stories fallback and its count, the hypotheses with their shares, end dates and holdouts, the Kronos pin and the V1 bootstrap seed (0x99e6dbc2, the first 32 bits of the hash this amends) are unchanged, and Spec-2 still names Spec-1 hash 59cfffbc601b82a9677e20a71bad2e2833f2acfc5d0e325d7e000cb0dd438b07. This amends Spec-2 hash 99e6dbc2c656006c3b0bcdc91108e919abd9bfafd421b74fd97c9c8c50d8fa38.
amendments.reason: The news-stories job had not passed since it started. Over three hours on 10 Nov 2026 its 241 GDELT requests ended 109 rate_limited (429), 54 parse_error (an empty object at HTTP 200), 49 upstream_5xx, 23 non_json, 4 timeout and 2 fetched. Each 429 or 5xx was retried after 1 and 2 seconds inside the 5-second spacing, which kept GDELT's one-request-per-5-seconds limit tripped: a coin took about 32 seconds, so only about 80 of the 169 queried coins fitted the 40-minute fetch budget against the 0.95 completeness check. And an empty object, GDELT's reply for a window with no matching article, always failed, so a quiet coin could never pass. No news count has been written. The queries, the allowlist, the counts and every other field are unchanged.

changes: activity rule publish_gate: Activity's numbers wait for 48 hours of green capture (the last 96 capture-markets slots passed); news-stories runs no longer gate publication (was 48 hours of green collectors, read as 96 capture slots and the last 48 settled news-stories runs).

activity rule news_not_collected (new): while no news-stories run scheduled in the 120 minutes before a reading's slot has passed, the news input is unknown at weight 0 with reason not_collected, as X is, and rejoins at the first reading after a news-stories run passes.

activity rule combination: A publishes with Trading activity measured; Attention and Leverage join when measured (was Attention and Trading activity both required), so a reading can publish while news is not collected.
amendments.disclosure: Spec-2 amendment 2 (11 Nov 2026), before any Activity reading was published and before any news count was written: Activity's 48-hour publish gate now reads capture-markets alone, and while the GDELT news collector is down a reading's news input is shown as not collected at weight 0, never carried forward, invented or read as 0, and rejoins automatically when news-stories passes again. A reading needs Trading activity; Attention and Leverage join when measured. The reason is GDELT's DOC API being overloaded for every caller (FI-32, owner decision of 11 Nov 2026). The news queries, the publisher allowlist, the stories fallback and its count, the percentiles and freshness rules, the hypotheses with their shares, end dates and holdouts, the Kronos pin and the V1 bootstrap seed (0x99e6dbc2) are unchanged, and Spec-2 still names Spec-1 hash 59cfffbc601b82a9677e20a71bad2e2833f2acfc5d0e325d7e000cb0dd438b07. This amends Spec-2 hash 04452fe7eb04502a202077b1500ef63af4538399d78cc01c24e4babc153e1f75.
amendments.reason: GDELT's DOC API, the only registered news source, has been overloaded for every caller: HTTP 429s and dropped connections, reproduced from outside our cluster as well as from it. The news-stories job therefore fails every run even after amendment 1's pacing, and under the registered gate Activity stayed Readings start for as long as GDELT stays down, with no reading ever published although capture-markets was green. Mena decided on 11 Nov 2026 (FI-32) that Activity publishes on capture alone, with news shown as not collected at weight 0 while it is down, as X counts already are. No news count has been written and no Activity reading has been published.

news.contextGroup: (crypto OR cryptocurrency OR token OR blockchain)

rules.rule: Each news-counts run (hourly at :10 UTC) counts the UTC hour that ended at the top of its slot's hour. It reads CryptoPanic's public English news posts newest first, page by page (20 a page on Growth), until a post published before that hour or the last page, at most 8 pages. A coin's hourly tally (news_cryptopanic_posts_1h) is the number of distinct posts published in the hour that carry its registered code as an instrument and, where a name is registered, an instrument title containing that name, case-folded. A failed request fails the hour; 8 pages that do not reach the hour's start truncate it; a failed or truncated hour leaves every coin's tally null with its reason, never 0.
An hour with no news post at all is null canary_zero for every coin: CryptoPanic carries news every hour, so an empty hour is read as a fault, never as zeros.
news_cryptopanic_posts_24h_1h at bucket b is the sum of the coin's 24 hourly tallies ending at b. An hour with no passed tally (missing) or a null tally makes it null with that hour's reason.

CryptoPanic publishes no list of the codes it tags, so a coin is covered once a post in the 30 days ending at b carried its code (and name, where registered). An uncovered coin's 24-hour input is null missing, shown as Not measured, never 0; a covered coin with no post in the 24 hours is a measured 0.

Growth allows 3,000 requests a month and 1 month of history. The client sends at most 2,900 a month (IL_CRYPTOPANIC_MONTHLY_REQUEST_CAP); a request refused at the cap fails its hour (quota). No news backfill is registered: Growth's history and quota cannot cover 90 days, so news history builds forward from the first run.

Counts only: no headline, description, link, publisher name or author from CryptoPanic is stored or shown, because its API terms give no licence to display third-party headlines commercially. Under owner decision FI-38 (12 Nov 2026) no page, API response, MCP reply, share card or method page names the source: the counts are described as news story counts.

news.queryRule: Per coin: its CoinGecko name (and the previous name CoinGecko gives in brackets) as quoted phrases, OR'd, plus its ticker only where both drafts kept it (at least 3 Latin characters and not an English word or a person's name); the context group follows unless the name has no other meaning in news (household names such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin). A coin whose name is a common English word that the context group cannot disambiguate gets no query and is listed as missing, unknown at weight 0. OR appears only inside brackets, a lone phrase is never bracketed, and no query exceeds 1,024 characters.

rules.rule: News counts come from allowlisted stories: for each coin, its query's article list from GDELT, kept only where the article's domain is on the publisher allowlist, one per domain per coin per 24 hours. The input news_allowlisted_stories_24h_1h is the number of distinct allowlisted domains with at least one such story in the 24 hours ending at the hourly bucket; live only.

In this mode gdelt_articles_1d is never written: backfilled news days are unmeasured at weight 0, and gdelt-backfill refuses with 'news backfill unmeasured (Spec-2)'. The live GDELT count job refuses with 'news counts come from the story counter (Spec-2)'; the story counter writes the live input.

Bitcoin's query is each batch's canary: a zero counts only from a parsed 200 whose same-batch bitcoin count is non-zero; a 429, a text body with HTTP 200 ('too short or too long', a rate-limit notice) or a timeout is a failed request and its window is null, never 0. An empty object at HTTP 200 is a fetched window with zero articles only when the same run's bitcoin request has already parsed with at least one article; otherwise (bitcoin's own empty object, or a run whose bitcoin request failed or parsed none) it is a failed request and its window is null, never 0.

One request per 10 seconds or slower from one egress, each a single attempt: a 429, a 5xx or a timeout fails its window at once with no retry, and the next request still waits its 10 seconds; no request between 23:00 and 00:30 UTC writes in a batch (the write governor).

A later probe that shows folded counts from the production egress can register allowlist_folded only at an epoch (A1.0's epoch 1, §4.2 step 10), with its own public hash before any news backfill; an allowlist folded into a query holds at most 8 domains (the probe's length limit).
Story links are rendered nofollow; headline, source and link only; stories are clustered across publishers before counting (REQ-18).

A coin that enters the evaluation universe after this registration has no registered news query: its news input is unknown at weight 0 with reason 'no registered query (Spec-2)', never 0 and never a query built at run time, until an epoch registers one.

publishers.rule: Both drafts' allowlists intersected (spec-2-reconcile.md): crypto newsrooms with editors and corrections policies, and the wires and business papers that cover crypto daily. A story counts only when its URL's registrable domain equals one of these exactly. The list changes only at an epoch.

social.decision: FI-36 (11 Nov 2026), Mena: "we have permission" to publish LunarCrush-derived data; recorded as the owner's permission, not read from LunarCrush's public terms.

emergingCheck.rule: Each social-counts run reads one extra coins/list/v2 page by market-cap rank, page 1 plus the run's UTC hour mod 6, unless the run already read it, and matches every row's blockchains[].address against Emerging tokens first seen in the last 30 days (case-folded for 0x addresses, exact otherwise). A match stores a token_seen snapshot at the run's hour, and an Emerging token page may say it was seen in social data when one was stored in the last 24 hours. Display only: it never enters a score, a stage, a band or a public-row check, and a failed extra page fails nothing.

rules.rule: Each social-counts run (hourly at :40 UTC) reads LunarCrush coins/list/v2 sorted by market-cap rank, 1,000 rows a page, from page 0, stopping once every registered code is found, at most 3 pages: at most 72 requests a day of the account's 2,000 (10 a minute, shared by every key). The client sends at most 1,500 a day (IL_LUNARCRUSH_DAILY_REQUEST_CAP).

A coin's row is the one whose symbol equals its registered code and, where a name is registered, whose name contains it, case-folded. When several rows match, the largest by market cap counts only when its market cap is at least ten times the next one's; otherwise the coin is not measured that hour. A coin with no row is not covered: not measured, never 0.

social_lunarcrush_posts_24h_1h at bucket b (the run's hour) is the row's social_volume_24h, LunarCrush's count of posts with interactions in the 24 hours before config.generated, which is its providerTime; a missing or negative value is null.

Counts and display facts only: no post, post text or creator from LunarCrush is stored or shown, and no vendor composite score is shown (rule vendor_scores). Under owner decision FI-38 (12 Nov 2026) no page, API response, MCP reply, share card or method page names the source: it is described as social activity.

Each social-counts run also stores, per matched coin at the run's hour, the list row's sentiment (the interaction-weighted share of positive posts, 0 to 100), social_dominance (the coin's share of all social volume, in percent), interactions_24h and categories in social_snapshots. Coin pages show the positive share, the share of social conversation and 24-hour interactions, and the home page a compact view, each measured, not measured (no matched row or no value, never 0) or collecting (no snapshot in the last 3 hours). They are display facts in no score.

galaxy_score and alt_rank are the vendor's own composite scores: they may be stored with a snapshot for evaluation only and are never shown, served or blended into any reading, because they cannot honestly be shown without naming their source.

social-trend (daily at 00:50 UTC) reads coins/:coin/time-series/v2 with bucket day for each registered coin whose newest snapshot in the last 7 days names its vendor id, from 8 days before the run's UTC day, and stores each complete UTC day's posts_created, posts_active, contributors_active, interactions and sentiment as a daily snapshot; coin pages show the last 7 complete days. A request the plan refuses (HTTP 401, 402 or 403) stores the coins' last complete day as not measured with reason access_refused and ends the run's reads; a coin with no vendor id is not measured. No value is carried forward or read as 0.
social-trend-backfill runs once and reads 90 days per coin in one request each, stored as daily snapshots with origin backfilled; it writes no registered input.

Requests a day: 24 to 72 coins/list pages for the input (rule read), 24 extra coins/list pages for the Emerging cross-check and about 169 time-series requests (one per coin), so at most about 265 a day, plus about 169 once for the backfill, of the account's 2,000. The client sends at most 1,500 a day (IL_LUNARCRUSH_DAILY_REQUEST_CAP).

shadow.rule: contributors_active (distinct accounts posting with interactions) and posts_created, from each daily snapshot, are Attention input candidates in shadow: each day social-trend computes each candidate's mid-rank percentile in the coin's own window of up to 90 days (unknown under 20 non-zero days) and stores it with that day's snapshot. They carry weight 0, enter no reading and are never published. social_lunarcrush_posts_24h_1h stays the registered input; replacing it with a candidate needs a later amendment that states the comparison.

queries.pattern: When X is added: one query per universe asset, its cashtag and its CoinGecko name as a quoted phrase, OR'd, then -is:retweet, at most 1,024 characters, holding no stoplisted term.
queries.reason: X post counts are not bought: FI-14 (nothing bought without Mena's word) and Mena's 'add x later'; ruling RC13 keeps X off until Mena says 'add X'. FI-15 lets X counts come from a third-party product; the X side run found no third-party product with per-query counts and kept the official X API, which needs Mena's spend. Until a later registration adds X, X counts are unknown at weight 0 and Attention reads from news alone.

x.rules: While X is not collected every X job refuses ('X counts not registered (Spec-2)') and no X row is written. 'Add X' needs a new registration with its own public hash (§3 Backfill rule) holding the query list, the stoplist, the settle lag of 15 minutes, a 6-hourly cadence where each call reads 7 days of hourly buckets, maxAge 8 hours, a per-coin coverage floor and bitcoin's query as the canary; the 90-day backfill from full-archive counts uses the identical query and starts after that hash is public. A coin that enters the evaluation universe after this registration has no registered X query: its X input is unknown at weight 0 with reason 'no registered query (Spec-2)', never 0 and never a query built at run time, until an epoch registers one.

stoplist.rule: The collision stoplist is reviewed on up to 500 recent counts (about US$2.50) when X is added, and registered with the query list in that registration, before any X fetch.

emerging.rule: Discovery uses neutral new-pool and trending feeds (CoinGecko /onchain, DexScreener pairs), never paid profiles or boosts; keyless DexScreener calls run at :07 and :37 UTC at half its per-address limit, clear of v1's radar scan.

Any asset in the current evaluation universe, by CoinGecko id or by chain and contract address, is excluded from Emerging; corroboration counts only by shared chain and contract address (REQ-08, FI-4).
First-seen time is stored. A public row needs a pool at least 24 hours old, at least US$50,000 liquidity, a passed honeypot check and top-10 holders under 80%; failures count only in survival totals.
A tracker looks up every token under 7 days old at each scan.

Lifecycle: New (pool under 24 hours old), Trading (a public row neither Fading nor Inactive), Fading (24-hour volume under 10% of its own peak since first seen, not Inactive), Inactive (every pool under US$1,000 liquidity and US$500 24-hour volume at two consecutive scans), Unobserved (the lookup failed).

The meme test is stored per token with classSource, classAt and ruleVersion: a reviewed launchpad or bonding-curve origin; no live mint or freeze authority; no staking, yield, reflection, fee-share, buyback, presale or vesting contract; not wrapped, bridged or tokenised; no return claims; no collision with a top-250 asset or a stoplisted brand. Any unknown answer means 'Not classed: facts only'.
Tokenised assets are excluded by chain and issuer lists, never by name.
Meme-class attention bands use unique-trader counts and volume-to-liquidity capped at 5 (the lower of the drafts' caps), measured parts only.

REQ-24's social velocity over a fixed 24 hours is unmeasured for new tokens (no licensed social source; X counts would cover reviewed majors only), unknown at weight 0, joining the 1 Mar 2027 social-tone yes or no.
Issuer text is never rendered; names leave the API and MCP only as an untrusted issuerName.
The Monday digest prints the meme test's pass share; an agent samples 20 tokens weekly; the survival record counts only fully looked-up tokens and prints coverage.
Discovery is forward only: no backfill of new pools, which would keep only the survivors.

One forecast a day per frozen major from Mon 9 Nov 2026: the last 400 closed hourly candles as context (the forming candle dropped), 24 sampled paths of 24 hourly steps, sampling settings recorded in each forecast row; the up probability is the share of paths whose final close is above the last close, and the 80% central interval comes from the paths' final closes by the Weibull plotting position.

The 20 frozen majors are the 20 largest universe coins by market cap at Spec-1's data pull that have at least two venues at US$1M or more in A-2c's field report (both drafts agreed); the list never changes during H5.

sections: 4.2 step 2 (venue allowlist, basis cross-check, contract map)
4.4 Validation (H-incl, H3, H0-dir, H4, H5, V1)

positioning.basisFinding: Confirmed: the registered input stays (price minus index) over index from the same ticker (Spec-1's cg_perp_premium_1h). A-2c's field report tested CoinGecko's basis against percent, fraction and both negations of that ratio on 28,115 perpetual rows and no venue matched any reading (best share 0.124 among large venues), so basis has no known unit or sign: it is stored as a cross-check only, and the 5-MAD drop and the Crowded flag run on (price minus index) over index, never on basis.

rules.rule: A contract drops at a snapshot when its price differs from its own index by more than 5% (priceBandFromIndex 0.05); the 15-minute last-trade age, expiry and 5-MAD rules of Spec-1 apply as registered there.

A venue's reading for a coin is the open-interest-weighted mean of (price minus index) over index over its surviving reviewed contracts for that coin (USDT, USDC, USD1, U and coin-margined alike); the venue's open interest is their sum, and Spec-1's 50% venue cap and two-venue, US$1M (in 1.2M, out 0.8M) rule apply to venues, not contracts.

Rows join to coins only through the reviewed contract map registered apart from this spec (src/registry/contract-map.ts and its own sha256): a reviewed entry maps, an unmapped one never does, and a row on a venue outside this allowlist never counts. A map correction before first light recomputes Positioning from stored rows with no seam; after first light only at an epoch.
Open interest is as each venue reports it, with no cross-check; the field report's unchecked mid-tier venues are outside the allowlist, and the 50% cap limits any one venue.

venues.rule: Both drafts' venue allowlists intersected (spec-2-reconcile.md). Draft A screened on breadth and freshness (at least 80 universe coins at US$1M or more, under 10% stale rows, median last-trade age at most 15 minutes, a non-zero funding field); draft B took the 15 largest by reported open interest less those the field report flags as unchecked (WEEX, OrangeX, CoinW, Tapbit), unjoinable (KuCoin), thin (under 50 coins) or stale. title: Interlucent Spec-2: Attention instruments, venue allowlist, A1.0, Unusual attention, Emerging, H-incl, H3, H0-dir, H4, H5 and V1

unusualAttention.rule: Unusual attention (REQ-21's name): Attention above its own 95th percentile in two consecutive non-overlapping 6-hour windows.

Corroborated in those windows by Trading activity above its own 80th percentile at both closes, or by social activity (rule social_corroboration). Stories from allowlisted publishers no longer corroborate: none is collected since amendment 3.

Social activity corroborates when the coin's 24-hour social post volume (social_volume_24h, the value of social_lunarcrush_posts_24h_1h) in its hourly social snapshot at the newest hour at or before the second close, fetched by the run's start and at most 2 hours before the close, is at least 2 times the median of its hourly snapshots at the same hour of day on the 30 days before, with at least 14 of those days stored and that median above 0. The ratio is stored with the row as socialActivityRatio, null when not measured, and is never carried forward or read as 0.
An uncorroborated spike appears only on the coin page ('X post spike, not corroborated' or 'News spike, not corroborated'), never on the home page, presets, the Weekly, alerts or IndexNow.

X-led spikes cannot occur while X is not collected. When a registration adds X, it also registers the sampled read of up to 100 posts (about US$0.50, IDs deleted within 24 hours), the author-diversity threshold for 'likely coordinated', and the day-8 vintage check whose ratios release the data-quality hold on promoted placements (coin pages keep the reading flagged 'backfilled counts as of' the backfill date).
News-led spikes need no vintage hold in stories_fallback mode, because the news input has no backfill; each bucket's first passed read is the registered value and later reads are stored as vintages.
The outcome log keeps persistence and first-seen time, never price outcomes; a manipulation audit goes to the Monday digest.

v1.rule: V1 is registered here, before the 200-item labelling pilot on Fri 6 Nov 2026.

Items are stratified, post-model-cutoff, entity-anonymised headlines from the live allowlisted, deduplicated stories, never backfilled GDELT, with about 200 adversarial items; a 200-item pilot, then about 2,000 items with three labels each on Prolific or Toloka.
Krippendorff's alpha of at least 0.67 among labellers, or the batch is relabelled.
One headline per call, abstention allowed; the classifier runs through llm-router after its 9 to 10 Nov rebuild (birch-config refuses direct AI keys).
Pass at macro-F1 at least 0.70 and at least 0.9 times human agreement, with a bootstrap lower bound of at least 0.65, on at least 500 held-out items never used to tune prompts or thresholds.
After a pass, published coins show 'News tone: Positive, Mixed or Negative' as a separate reading with Tone maxAge 26 hours; Tone enters a score only at an epoch (no earlier than 1 Mar 2027).
